subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw grow a true soft-steer lifecycle that can pause or abort active generation/tool work, inject new user input, and resume, or should it keep steering limited to runtime/model boundaries plus the existing interrupt mode?
rationale: Current main already has a narrower active-run steering improvement, but the requested behavior changes core run lifecycle and failure semantics rather than filling a small implementation gap.

options.title: Design soft-steer explicitly
options.body: Keep this issue open as the tracker and require a maintainer-sponsored design before landing runtime changes.

options.title: Keep boundary steering
options.body: Close or narrow this request after documenting that immediate mid-generation pause/resume is intentionally out of scope.

options.title: Land only the narrow subset
options.body: Treat active non-streaming queue injection as the only supported improvement and track true pause/resume separately.

recommendation.title: Design soft-steer explicitly
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the tracker and require a maintainer-sponsored design before landing runtime changes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the latest current-main blame on the relevant steer gates and already supplied maintainer review context on this issue.
